newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville expands power offer to SW at $9/MWh.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville expands power offer to SW at $9/MWh.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) expanded its offer to sell non-firm power during light-load hours on Thursday at $9.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) to include Southwest transmissions, BPA said Wednesday.
The offer applies only to buyers willing to displace thermal generation with BPA's hydroelectric power.
For Wednesday pre-scheduled sales, BPA offered that price to Northwest buyers only. The agency continued to offer Northwest-only power at prices as low at $7.00 per Mwh.

BPA's offers for daily surplus firm and non-firm power were unchanged at $17.00 per MWh between 1300 and 2100 PDT, $14.50 for hours 0800-1200 and 2200-2300, and $13.00 for hours 0100-0700 and the hour ending 2400.
Electricity market sources said the Northwest continues to generate excess supplies of hydroelectric power at the same time regional demand is flagging due to cooler weather.
